item.title: Beneath the Surface
item.description:
Beneath the Surface

2024 · Installation Series
Medium: Mordançage photography on fiber paper, mixed media
Dimensions: Variable, approximately 20 works

An exploration of consumer spaces through mordançage photography, examining the tension between commercial aspiration and economic reality through chemically manipulated photographic prints.

Exhibition History

Art for All Festival

Easton Mall, Columbus, OH · August 2024

Solo exhibition featuring approximately 20 mordançage prints installed in an abandoned mall space during the Art for All festival. The work was created under intense time pressure, with the entire process—from shooting to installation—completed in approximately one week.

Artistic Process

The series emerged from an intense week-long creative sprint, beginning with photographing the Easton Mall spaces and culminating in a full installation. This compressed timeline became integral to the work’s conceptual framework, mirroring the pressure and urgency of commercial cycles.

Production Timeline

  • Day 1-2: Location photography (2 rolls of film)
  • Day 3-4: Film processing and contact printing
  • Day 5-6: Production printing (~50 prints total)
  • Day 6-7: Mordançage treatment (20 selected prints)
  • Day 7: Framing and installation

Technical Notes

The mordançage process involves treating developed silver gelatin prints with a bleaching solution that softens the emulsion, allowing it to be physically manipulated, stretched, or removed from the paper base. This technique, dating to the 19th century, creates unique textures and surface qualities impossible to achieve through digital means.

Conceptual Framework

Beneath the Surface operates on multiple levels of meaning:

Physical Transformation: The mordançage process literally transforms the photographic surface, paralleling the economic and social transformations affecting retail spaces.

Temporal Pressure: The compressed production timeline reflected the urgent, speculative nature of commercial development and its equally rapid obsolescence.

Spatial Context: Exhibiting in the abandoned Easton Mall created a direct dialogue between the work and its subject matter, with the installation inhabiting the same type of space it critiques.

Documentation and Reception

The work was documented extensively during both production and exhibition phases. The intense timeline and alternative venue contributed to strong engagement from festival audiences, many of whom were experiencing mordançage processes for the first time.

Related Works

This series connects to broader themes explored in my practice:

  • Mordançage Experiments - The foundational technical explorations
  • Quantum Mordançage Zine - Conceptual expansion into print media

For more information about this work or inquiries about exhibitions, please contact me.

item.title: Quantum Mordançage Zine
item.description:
Quantum Mordançage Zine

2024 · Limited Edition Artist’s Zine
Medium: Risograph printing, hand-folded
Edition: Limited run, ongoing distribution
Dimensions: Standard zine format

A limited-edition artist’s zine exploring the intersection of quantum mechanics and photographic chemistry through mordançage processes. Each copy is hand-folded and distributed through alternative art networks and direct engagement.

Concept and Development

The zine emerged from conceptual connections between quantum mechanical principles and the mordançage photographic process. Both involve states of transformation, uncertainty, and the observer’s role in determining outcomes. The publication serves as both documentation and theoretical exploration of these parallels.

Thematic Connections

Quantum Superposition ↔ Photographic Latent Image: Both exist in states of potential until observation/development

Wave-Particle Duality ↔ Mordançage Transformation: Matter existing in multiple states simultaneously

Observer Effect ↔ Chemical Manipulation: The act of observation/interaction fundamentally changes the system

Production Process

The zine was produced using risograph printing, chosen for its mechanical unpredictability that mirrors the chance elements in both quantum mechanics and mordançage chemistry.

Hand-Folding Process

Each zine is individually hand-folded, making every copy slightly unique despite being printed from the same masters. This manual process reinforces the handmade, alternative nature of the publication.

Content and Structure

The zine combines theoretical text, process documentation, and visual examples to create a comprehensive exploration of the quantum-photographic parallels. Content includes:

  • Theoretical framework connecting quantum mechanics and photography
  • Technical documentation of mordançage processes
  • Visual examples showing transformation states
  • Conceptual diagrams illustrating quantum-photographic analogies

Distribution and Reception

The zine circulates through alternative art networks, including:

  • Direct sales at exhibitions and events
  • Mail art exchanges
  • Independent bookstores specializing in artist publications
  • Academic conferences on alternative processes

The publication has found audiences among both photographers interested in alternative processes and readers engaged with experimental art theory.

Significance in Practice

The zine represents an expansion of my practice into publication and theoretical writing. It serves multiple functions:

Documentation: Recording and sharing technical knowledge about mordançage Theory Development: Exploring conceptual frameworks for understanding alternative processes
Community Building: Connecting with others working at the intersection of art and science Alternative Distribution: Engaging with networks outside traditional gallery systems

Technical Specifications

Printing: Risograph, multiple ink colors
Paper: Standard zine paper stock
Binding: Hand-folded, saddle-stitched
Edition Size: Limited run, exact numbers available upon request
Distribution: Ongoing through multiple channels

Related Works

This publication connects to broader themes in my practice:

  • Beneath the Surface - Practical application of mordançage techniques documented in the zine
  • Experiments blog - Ongoing documentation of alternative process work

Availability: For information about obtaining a copy or questions about the publication, please contact me.

item.title: Mordançage Experiments
item.description:
Mordançage Experiments

2024 · Foundational Research Series
Medium: Mordançage on silver gelatin prints
Status: Foundation for exhibition work

Initial explorations of the mordançage process that established the technical and conceptual framework for later exhibition works. These experiments investigate the physical transformation of photographic emulsion and its potential for expressing themes of vulnerability and change.

Process Development

This body of work represents the foundational research phase of my mordançage practice. Through systematic experimentation with different papers, chemicals, and manipulation techniques, I developed the methods later employed in exhibition works like Beneath the Surface.

Technical Discoveries

The mordançage process involves treating developed silver gelatin prints with a bleaching solution that softens the photographic emulsion, allowing it to be physically manipulated. Key technical insights from this experimental phase include:

  • Paper selection: Different fiber papers respond uniquely to mordançage treatment
  • Timing variations: Emulsion manipulation windows vary with temperature and solution strength
  • Surface effects: Various manipulation techniques create distinct textural qualities
  • Drying considerations: Different drying methods affect final surface characteristics

Conceptual Framework

Beyond technical mastery, these experiments established the conceptual foundation for using mordançage as a metaphor for transformation and vulnerability. The process became a way to explore:

Physical Vulnerability: The photographic surface becomes literally fragile and manipulable
Temporal Transformation: Images change through time and chemical action
Chance and Control: The balance between intentional manipulation and unpredictable chemical reactions
Material Honesty: Embracing the physical properties of photographic materials

Documentation and Process

This experimental phase was extensively documented to establish reproducible methods for later exhibition work. The systematic approach allowed for consistent results when working under the time pressure of exhibition deadlines.

The learnings from these experiments directly informed:

  • Production methods for Beneath the Surface
  • Process documentation in Quantum Mordançage Zine
  • Technical approaches for future exhibition work

Significance in Practice

While these experiments may appear as individual studies, they function as the foundation for my entire mordançage-based practice. Each technical discovery and conceptual insight developed here enabled the rapid, confident execution of later exhibition work.

This foundational research phase demonstrates the importance of sustained experimental work in developing both technical fluency and conceptual clarity before moving to public presentation.

Related Works

This foundational work connects to:

  • Beneath the Surface - First major exhibition application
  • Quantum Mordançage Zine - Conceptual development and documentation

For ongoing experimental work in other processes (lith printing, sabattier effect, etc.), see the Experiments blog section.

For more information about this foundational work or technical inquiries, please contact me.
